Subject: SIG follow-up — encryption details request

Hi Irene / Jonas,

Thanks for taking our SIG intake earlier this week. SafeBox is working through vendor encryption controls for our procurement review. We have a few targeted asks to finalize Section 6 (Encryption & Key Management):

- In-transit: TLS versions supported, cipher suites, whether mutual TLS is used for service-to-service traffic.
- At-rest: algorithms, modes (AEAD vs. CBC), envelope encryption design (DEKs/KEKs).
- KMS/HSM: vendor(s) used, single-tenant vs shared HSMs, attestations available.
- Key rotation: rotation cadence for KEKs and DEKs, automatic vs manual rotation, procedures for emergency (compromise) rotation.
- Customer-managed keys: do you support BYOK, and what steps are required?

Can you provide a short one-page topology diagram and the specific SIG cells that describe the above? If possible we'd like a 30-min technical walkthrough (recorded) and the supporting artifacts by EOD next week.

Attached is our intake reference and the specific SIG rows we flagged. Let us know next-available times — mornings (US ET) work best for us.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — encryption details request (topology & rotation summary)

Samir — attaching the requested artifacts and summarizing answers inline. Attachments: kms-hsm-topology-2027.pdf, kek_rotation_schedule.csv, transit_tls_profiles.md.

Quick summary (answers to your bullets):

1) In-transit
- All customer-facing APIs and internal service traffic require TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 preferred. We support modern AEAD cipher suites (e.g., TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256).
- Service-to-service traffic inside our VPC uses mTLS for control plane communications; customer API traffic is TLS (client TLS certificate optional for dedicated/private deployments).

2) At-rest
- Data-at-rest is encrypted using AES-256-GCM. We employ envelope encryption: per-object data encryption keys (DEKs) are AES-256 keys; DEKs are wrapped by key-encryption-keys (KEKs).
- DEKs are stored encrypted and only unwrapped by authorized services with appropriate IAM roles and least privilege.

3) KMS / HSM topology & vendor
- KEKs are stored in an HSM-backed KMS. Our primary deployment uses AWS KMS with a custom key store backed by Amazon CloudHSM (FIPS 140-2 validated). For select private/on-prem customers we support on-prem HSMs (PKCS#11-compatible) integrated via our control plane.
- KEKs live in an HSM cluster that is multi-tenant at the HSM hardware level but isolated through dedicated CloudHSM partitions where required; we can provide dedicated HSM clusters for enterprise customers under a separate engagement.

4) Key rotation & lifecycle
- DEKs: rotated automatically every 90 days by default. Applications use a key-id reference; old DEKs are retained for decrypting existing ciphertexts until data re-encryption or expiry.
- KEKs (root/wrapping keys): rotated on an annual cadence (365 days) by default. We also support manual rotation and emergency rotation playbooks if compromise is suspected. Rotation is implemented as a double-wrap / re-wrap operation to avoid mass re-encryption at rotation time.
- Key compromise: documented incident runbook (we'll provide the runbook in the secure package) — steps include immediate key disabling in KMS, rotation of KEKs, replay token invalidation, and coordinated customer notifications if customer keys are affected.

5) Customer-managed keys (BYOK)
- Supported: customers can bring keys via cloud KMS import or connect an external HSM (PKCS#11) in private/dedicated deployments. For hosted customers we provide a BYOK option through AWS KMS import or CMKs stored in a dedicated custom key store.

6) Backup & escrow
- Key backups are stored as HSM-wrapped exports and are encrypted and access-controlled. For CloudHSM-based keys we maintain encrypted backups in region-limited object storage; restore requires multi-person approval.

7) Audit & attestation
- All key operations (create/rotate/disable/describe/decrypt) are logged to our immutable audit pipeline and retained per the customer's retention tier. We can provide CloudHSM attestation details and our SOC 2 report under NDA.

Attachments included in secure Drive link: kms-hsm-topology-2027.pdf (topology diagram), kek_rotation_schedule.csv (example rotation cadence / sample dates), transit_tls_profiles.md (list of supported TLS cipher suites and config snippets).

I'll drop the meeting invite for Thu Jun 17 16:00 ET and include a short agenda (SIG walkthrough + Q&A + artifacts walk-through). If you need dedicated HSMs or a signed attestation sooner, let us know and we'll prioritize.

Regards,
